Frequently asked
questions
Choose a ready-made, lightly adapted, or fully tailored version.
Games and AI-scored interviews use AI. The Virtual Job Tryout does not.
Outputs vary by assessment and can include scores, fit, strengths, and recommended follow-up questions.
Pre-employment assessment software helps employers evaluate candidates using structured, job-relevant exercises. Hirevue Assessments measure skills, cognitive abilities, behaviours, language proficiency, coding ability, and job readiness to help predict workplace success.
A Virtual Job Tryout, or VJT assessment, is a realistic job simulation that allows candidates to experience common tasks and scenarios associated with a role. Employers use Virtual Job Tryouts to evaluate judgment, decision-making, and job fit before hiring.
Virtual Job Tryout questions and exercises vary by role. Candidates may respond to workplace scenarios, prioritise tasks, solve problems, or demonstrate how they would handle situations they could encounter on the job.
A game-based assessment uses short, interactive tasks to measure job-relevant cognitive and behavioural skills. Hirevue Game-Based Assessments can help employers consistently evaluate abilities such as problem-solving, attention, memory, and learning agility.
Hirevue game-based assessments compare candidate performance with predefined, job-relevant criteria. Results help recruiters understand a candidate’s strengths and potential fit, while employers retain control over advancement and final hiring decisions.
A coding assessment evaluates a candidate’s technical ability through practical programming exercises. Coding assessments help employers verify skills earlier in the hiring process rather than relying only on resumes or self-reported experience.
A coding assessment platform can evaluate programming knowledge, problem-solving, code quality, and role-specific technical skills. Hirevue coding assessments and technical assessments automatically score exercises and provide recruiters with consistent candidate insights.
Yes. Organisations can choose ready-made assessments, lightly customise existing content, or create tailored assessments based on the role, required skills, and desired performance outcomes.
AI may be used to score certain games and structured video responses. Other assessment types like the Virtual Job Tryout simulation, use established scoring methods without AI. Recruiters remain responsible for advancement and hiring decisions.
Outputs vary by assessment and may include scores, indicators of job fit, candidate strengths, and recommended interview questions. These insights help recruiters prioritise candidates and make more consistent, informed decisions.
